method.pick_rate: picked / shown (shown = agent passed the slot)
method.by_ocean_segment: trait >= 0.5 is high, else low (agent's jittered OCEAN)

notice_model.formula: p_notice = sigmoid(alpha0 + alpha_row[row] + alpha_f*ln(min(facings,cap)) + alpha_c*(centrality-1) + mission + time + sum(OCEAN terms))

p_ref_eye_centre_1facing.source: assumption: baseline chance a shopper notices one product at eye level, centre, 1 facing, on a unit relevant to their mission. Sits between the skeptic-calibrated persona eye-level priors (0.55-0.80, data/personas/staged_personas_v1.json verdict.sim_parameters.p_notice_eye_level). When a persona carries its own p_notice_eye_level it replaces this value (see persona_eye_override).

eye_vs_bottom_sales_ratio.source: Eye level vs worst shelf height = +39% sales. research/04-3d-sim-evidence-and-tech.md section 1, citing the field study in https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Planogram
eye_vs_bottom_sales_ratio.derivation: Assumes the full sales gap runs through noticing (Chandon et al. 2009, J. Marketing 73(6), https://journals.sagepub.com/doi/10.1509/jmkg.73.6.1: the shelf effects act through attention). p_bottom = p_ref / 1.39, so alpha_row.bottom = logit(p_bottom) - logit(p_ref).

top_vs_bottom_notice_ratio.source: Top shelf is 17% more likely to be noticed than bottom (20% more likely chosen). research/04-3d-sim-evidence-and-tech.md section 1; matches Chandon et al. 2009 https://journals.sagepub.com/doi/10.1509/jmkg.73.6.1
top_vs_bottom_notice_ratio.derivation: p_top = p_bottom * 1.17, so alpha_row.top = logit(p_top) - logit(p_ref).

facings_elasticity.source: Mean shelf-space elasticity 0.17 across 1,268 estimates (Eisend 2014, J. Retailing meta-analysis), summarised at https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Planogram; research/04-3d-sim-evidence-and-tech.md section 1
facings_elasticity.derivation: In p = sigmoid(... + alpha_f * ln(facings)), dln(p)/dln(facings) = alpha_f * (1 - p). Setting this to 0.17 at p_ref gives alpha_f = 0.17 / (1 - p_ref). Diminishing returns come from the log and the sigmoid ceiling, as in Drèze, Hoch & Purk 1994 (J. Retailing).

facings_cap.source: assumption: Drèze, Hoch & Purk 1994 found facings changes of about ±50% had little effect above a minimum threshold (research/04 section 1), so ln(facings) is capped at 6 facings to stop the optimiser buying lift with absurd space.

centre_vs_edge_ratio.source: Best vs worst horizontal position gives about +15% (research/04-3d-sim-evidence-and-tech.md section 3 calibration target). Direction from Atalay, Bodur & Rasolofoarison 2012, JCR 39(4), https://academic.oup.com/jcr/article/39/4/848/1798003 (central gaze cascade)
centre_vs_edge_ratio.derivation: alpha_c = logit(p_ref) - logit(p_ref / 1.15). centrality runs 0 (edge of the slot set) to 1 (centre). The term is alpha_c * (centrality - 1), so the centre is the reference.

mission_relevance_logit.source: assumption: a unit outside the shopper's mission is browsed, not searched. Goal-directed (top-down) attention raises noticing (Chandon et al. 2009 separate top-down from bottom-up effects), but no paper here gives the size. -0.8 logit roughly halves the odds while browsing. Flagged as unsourced magnitude.

seconds_at_shelf_logit_per_ln.source: assumption: more seconds at the shelf means more fixations, so more products get noticed. Per-persona seconds_at_shelf come from the skeptic-calibrated params (data/personas/staged_personas_v1.json verdict.sim_parameters.seconds_at_shelf). The 0.25 per ln(seconds/6) slope is unsourced.

persona_eye_override.source: When a persona carries sim_parameters.p_notice_eye_level (skeptic-calibrated, data/personas/staged_personas_v1.json), alpha0 = logit(that value). The literature row, facings and centre offsets are then applied on top, so the persona sets the level and the literature sets the shape.

ocean_jitter_sd.source: assumption: each spawned agent gets its persona's OCEAN plus N(0, 0.08) noise, clipped to 0-1, so agents of one archetype are not clones. The size is a choice, not a measurement.

browse_prob.source: assumption: chance a shopper walks an off-mission unit. Unplanned buying is common, but no aisle-level visit rate is sourced here (research/04 section 3: 'give each item walked past a small impulse probability').

ocean_effects.effect: Conscientiousness lowers impulse noticing of off-mission products
ocean_effects.sim_mapping: sim/notice.py: coef * C_z added to the p_notice logit only when the product is off-mission (on_mission=False). r=-.18 -> d=-.366 -> logOR -.66 per SD; x0.4 shrink (assumption: survey impulse-buying tendency, not observed noticing) -> -0.27, rounded to -0.25.
ocean_effects.source: Personality puzzle: a comprehensive analysis of its impact on three buying behaviors. Frontiers in Psychiatry 2023;14:1179257. doi:10.3389/fpsyt.2023.1179257, PMC10475610 (r=-.18; beta=-.15, CI -.28 to -.07). Verplanken B, Herabadi A (2001). Individual differences in impulse buying tendency: feeling and no thinking. European Journal of Personality 15:S71-S83. doi:10.1002/per.423. Sci Rep 2025 doi:

ocean_effects.effect: label/read stage: Conscientiousness raises chance of reading the nutrition label (inferred via health interest)
ocean_effects.sim_mapping: label/read stage: p_read_label = sigma(logit(0.27) + coef*C_z) = sigma(-0.99 + 0.25*C_z). That gives 22% at -1 SD, 27% at the mean and 32% at +1 SD. The baseline is sourced. The 0.25 is an assumption (about logOR .365 from r=.10, shrunk by 0.7 because the path is inferred), ROUNDED UP to keep the RE
ocean_effects.source: Baseline: Grunert KG, Wills JM, Fernandez-Celemin L (2010). Nutrition knowledge, and use and understanding of nutrition information on food labels among consumers in the UK. Appetite 55(2):177-189. doi:10.1016/j.appet.2010.05.045. Trait link: Mottus et al. 2012 doi:10.1037/a0027041. Magnitude: assumption: no published C-to-label-use r found; inferred path, shrink stated.

ocean_effects.effect: External eating (eating in response to food cues: sight/smell/display) -> more sweet & savoury snacks, soft drinks and m
ocean_effects.sim_mapping: (a) notice alpha_trait for products with strong visual food cues (promo end, eye-level HFSS, OFF nutriscore_grade d/e in categories snacks/confectionery/soft drinks): + coef * z_E. Derivation: beta .05 ~ r .05 -> d .10 -> logit .18; NO attenuation applied because external eating is itself a cue-resp
ocean_effects.source: Keller, C., & Siegrist, M. (2015). Does personality influence eating styles and food choices? Direct and indirect effects. Appetite, 84, 128-138. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.appet.2014.10.003 (PMID 25308432; abstract: 'Extraversion promoted sweet and savory, meat and soft drink consumption via promoting external eating')

ocean_effects.effect: Social media / TikTok-Instagram exposure -> 'seen it online' familiarity with viral or novelty SKUs
ocean_effects.sim_mapping: notice alpha_trait for products flagged trending/novelty (e.g. lens archetype novelty_seeker_tiktok, or OFF 'new' / limited edition in product_name): + coef * z_E. Derivation: r=.10 -> d=.20 -> logit .36 -> x0.3 = 0.11, rounded 0.10. Reddit grounding of the mechanism: 'my system lately has been scro
ocean_effects.source: Liu, D., & Campbell, W. K. (2017). The Big Five personality traits, Big Two metatraits and social media: A meta-analysis. Journal of Research in Personality, 70, 229-240. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jrp.2017.08.004 (preprint https://doi.org/10.31234/osf.io/9bbns)

ocean_effects.effect: Brand-as-reward: favourite (chocolate) brands activate ventral striatum more strongly in more extraverted people
ocean_effects.sim_mapping: notice alpha_trait for brands already in the agent's habits/favourites list: + coef * z_E. Kept very small because of tiny-N fMRI evidence (assumption: 0.05 logit, roughly a quarter of the impulse effect).
ocean_effects.source: Schaefer, M., Knuth, M., & Rumpel, F. (2011). Striatal response to favorite brands as a function of neuroticism and extraversion. Brain Research, 1425, 83-89. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.brainres.2011.09.055 (PMID 22035566)

ocean_effects.effect: Label reading / deliberation (dwell on nutrition panel, number of attributes cited)
ocean_effects.sim_mapping: notice/attention to nutrition fields (OFF nutriments, nutriscore_grade) for high-E agents: coef * z_E with coef -0.05 (assumption: deliberately tiny; Conscientiousness, not E, should carry label attention per CONTRACT example).
ocean_effects.source: assumption: no direct study found; directional support from Verplanken & Herabadi (2001) https://doi.org/10.1002/per.423

ocean_effects.effect: Health anxiety -> more attention to 'warning' attributes (additives, allergens, 'ultra-processed', E-numbers, sugar/salt
ocean_effects.sim_mapping: notice: alpha_trait for 'warning' attributes (additives_n, allergens, nova_group=4, high-sugar/salt traffic lights) += 0.10*n_c, meaning more likely to notice and cite them. Lens: weight on additives_n/nova_group *= (1 + 0.10*n_c). Kept small because the N -> label-reading link is inferred, not dire
ocean_effects.source: Ferguson E (2000) Hypochondriacal concerns and the five factor model of personality. Journal of Personality 68(4):705-724, https://doi.org/10.1111/1467-6494.00113 (PMID 10934687)

ocean_effects.sim_mapping: sim/notice.py: alpha_trait_novel * O_z added to the p_notice logit only when the product is 'unfamiliar' to the agent (brand not in persona habits[], or OFF created_t within the last 18 months, or a challenger brand flagged in the store layout). r=-.23 -> d=.47 -> logOR .86/SD; x0.3 shrink because n
ocean_effects.source: Knaapila A, Silventoinen K, Broms U, Rose RJ, Perola M, Kaprio J, Tuorila HM (2011). Food neophobia in young adults: genetic architecture and relation to personality... a twin study. Behavior Genetics 41(4). doi:10.1007/s10519-010-9403-8

mission_categories._source: assumption: which store units each mission sends a shopper to; built from the mission descriptions in data/personas/staged_personas_v1.json (e.g. meal deal = main+snack+drink). A persona can override with mission_categories.
